high_entropy_sections.name: .idata
high_entropy_sections.justification: Section '.idata' has entropy 7.99 (>7.5). This is characteristic of encrypted or packed data. Typical compiled code sections have entropy between 5.5-6.5. Values above 7.5 are uncommon for standard executables and strongly suggest the presence of encrypted content or packing.

suspicious_entropy.name: .text
suspicious_entropy.justification: Section '.text' has entropy 6.63 (6.0-7.5). This is moderately high and may indicate obfuscated or compressed data. While this could be legitimate (e.g., resource data), in the context of malware it often suggests packing or string obfuscation.

suspicious_entropy.name: .rdata
suspicious_entropy.justification: Section '.rdata' has entropy 6.09 (6.0-7.5). This is moderately high and may indicate obfuscated or compressed data. While this could be legitimate (e.g., resource data), in the context of malware it often suggests packing or string obfuscation.

entropy_analysis.justification: Overall file entropy is 6.73, which is moderately high. This suggests the presence of obfuscated or compressed data. Found 1 sections with entropy >7.5 and 2 sections with entropy 6.0-7.5.
